summary: Household: New York; 6 people (you, your partner (married), 2 children under 18, your mom, and your dad, age 72); about $205,900 a year in combined work income; you own your home. Based on the 2026 rules, the household's income is above the limits for all ten programmes, so I don't recommend applying for any of them. SNAP, WIC, TANF, school meals and EITC all have income cutoffs well below this. SSI and Medicaid for your dad (and any Medicaid or NY Child Health Plus for the children) are income-tested far below this level. The ACA premium tax credit ends at 400% of the federal poverty level (about $172,600 for 6 people in 2025 figures), and the refundable part of the Child Tax Credit only pays out when a family owes little or no tax, which is unlikely at this income. The 2026 figures are my estimates, so if your income drops (for example, from a job loss or a large drop in hours) or your household changes, please rescreen.
